🇲🇽💜 <u>MEXICO CITY ENACTS A CARE SYSTEM LAW — FIRST OF ITS KIND</u>

Clara Brugada promulgated a Care System Law that treats childcare, eldercare and self-care as a collective responsibility — not the unpaid duty of women. It builds, in her words, "a welfare state with a feminist perspective," and for the first time puts a peso value on domestic labor in Mexico City, delivered on the ground through the Utopías and Casas de las Tres R. The care economy — the work that held everything up while going uncounted — finally gets counted.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>150 BILLION PESOS INTO THE GRID — PUBLIC POWER, PUBLIC WIRES</u>

Sheinbaum is putting 150 billion pesos into transmission and distribution, because "most interruptions come from overloaded lines," not a shortage of generation. After AMLO rebuilt public generating capacity through the CFE, the state is now modernizing the wires that carry that power to homes and businesses. Reliable electricity treated as a public good — financed and built by the state, not auctioned off.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO REJECTS NEW CHINA TRADE DEAL — ON ITS OWN TERMS</u>

Ebrard confirmed Mexico is not pursuing new free-trade agreements "not only with China, but with other countries" right now. It's not a snub — it's a strategy. Rather than swap dependence on US imports for dependence on Asian ones, Mexico is betting on Plan México and rebuilding its own productive capacity. Washington keeps calling Mexico a "backdoor for China"; the government's answer is to be nobody's backdoor and nobody's vassal — and to choose its own lane.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>LOZOYA'S SISTER ARRESTED — 5 MILLION DOLLARS, A SWISS ACCOUNT, A MANSION</u>

The FGR arrested Gilda Susana Lozoya at Mexico City's airport — sister of Peña Nieto's Pemex chief Emilio Lozoya. Per the Financial Intelligence Unit, she was legal front for the shell company Tochos Holding Limited and ran a Swiss bank account through which more than 5 million dollars moved to buy Emilio's mansion in Lomas de Bezares — money the FGR traces to bribes in the Agronitrogenados case. A triangulation scheme, they say, with no valid commercial justification. The graft file from the old regime is still being pulled apart, one prestanombre at a time.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO'S LIMES REACH RUSSIA — DIVERSIFICATION IN A CONTAINER</u>

Papantla, Veracruz just shipped its first 21.4 tonnes of Persian lime to Russia — 183 smallholders in the Bioproductores del Llano Alto co-op, selected because their fruit survives a 30-day sea voyage without losing its deep green. Volume is set to reach 257 tonnes in the second half of 2026. While Washington rattles tariffs, Mexican farmers are quietly opening a Eurasian market on their own. Trade diversification isn't a slogan — it's a container ship already at sea.

🇲🇽⚖️ The headlines called it a setback. Sheinbaum called it continuity. "If the US decides today not to extend 16 years, the treaty holds for the next 10 — its term to 2036 — and it's reviewed every year." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 Washington's refusal to extend USMCA to 2042 was read abroad as a loss. Mexico read it as the deal simply continuing on its own terms. It goes into the July 20 review with three aims: cut external dependency, fix review timelines, clarify the process. Negotiating from calm, not urgency.

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico is going to have a very important opportunity in these years." "The US is changing its trade relationship with every country… I think Mexico will have a very important opportunity these years." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 As Washington reshuffles its trade ties, South Korea, Japan and Canada have signaled interest in deeper commercial links with Mexico. Diversification isn't a threat — it's leverage.

🇲🇽⚽ The UK warned its fans away from seven Mexican states. Sheinbaum: "It's safe to visit the country." "It is safe to visit the country; they have no problem." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 Britain issued a travel alert ahead of the Mexico–England match on July 5. Sheinbaum pushed back plainly. On Mexico City's Reforma, where four people died in Tuesday's celebrations, the city is adding screens to spread out crowds. World Cup 2026 plays on.
